items.stem: Why should you double-quote a variable expansion like "$file" in Bash?

options.text: To prevent word splitting and glob expansion when the value contains spaces or wildcards
options.rationale: Unquoted expansions are split on whitespace and globbed, breaking paths.

options.text: Because single quotes also expand variables
options.rationale: Single quotes do not expand variables; double quotes do.
Quoting does not make a variable read-only.

options.text: Because Bash cannot read unquoted variables at all
options.rationale: It reads them, but may split/glob the result.

items.explanation: Unquoted expansions are split on whitespace and globbed, breaking paths.

items.stem: Select TWO correct statements about redirection in Bash.

options.rationale: A single > replaces the file's contents.
Double >> adds to the end without truncating.
2>&1 sends stderr to wherever stdout currently points.

options.text: A pipe | connects a command's stdin to the previous stdout's error stream
options.rationale: A pipe connects stdout of one to stdin of the next, not stderr.

items.explanation: A single > replaces the file's contents.
